correctness.rationale: Integrating the bridge kernel gives the piecewise cross-covariance for the derivative reading, prior trajectory risk 1/30, and area covariance t(1-t)/2. Squaring and integrating the cross-covariance gives the stated F, independently verified along with the derivative and high-noise gain ratio. The cubic f has one root in (2/5,5/12): it decreases to its only critical point in (0,1) and is negative from that minimum through 1. The noise coefficient changes sign at alpha; between beta and alpha both A and B_* increase strictly, while outside that interval their signs agree. Hence the derivative of the gain changes from positive to negative at exactly one interior time, with neither observation endpoint informative. Implicit differentiation gives positive noise sensitivity and simple-root Taylor expansions at zero and inverse noise zero. The terminal-area gain is strictly increasing in t(1-t), which is uniquely maximal at the midpoint; the high-noise path gain ratio is F(alpha)/F(1/2), not a ratio of posterior risks.
residual_risks: Limited to a single deterministic derivative observation under the normalized bridge model. The approximate 2.23% is a limiting relative increase in explained variance, not in the total posterior risk.
